meta.title_plain: Make your first Roblox script that opens a door
meta.teaser: Five steps to write Luau code that changes colours, vanishes platforms and opens doors.

page.title: Make your first Roblox script that opens a door
page.sub: A skill you can use today
page.bigIdea: Every Roblox game runs on a few lines of Luau. Alex Balfanz started coding on Roblox at 9 and later built Jailbreak, so your first lines count.

cards.title: Make a part, add a script
cards.front: Where does code live in Roblox Studio?
cards.back: Insert a Part, then set Anchored to true so it won't fall. Click the + next to it in the Explorer and add a Script. Rename both straight away.
cards.tryit: Open Roblox Studio, make one Part called MyDoor and put a Script inside it.

cards.title: Give it a name
cards.front: How does your script find its own part?
cards.back: Delete the starter code and type: local door = script.Parent. Now the word door means the part your script sits inside. That's a variable.
cards.tryit: Write the variable line, then add print(door.Name) and press Play. Check the Output window.

cards.title: Change a property
cards.front: How do you make a part vanish with code?
cards.back: Properties use a dot and an equals sign. door.Transparency = 1 makes it invisible. door.CanCollide = false lets players walk through it, like a ghost.
cards.tryit: Try Transparency values like 0.5 and 1. Then try door.Color = Color3.fromRGB(255, 0, 0).

cards.title: Group and repeat
cards.front: How do platforms vanish again and again?
cards.back: Put your lines in a function, like local function open(). A while true do loop repeats it. Always add task.wait(3), or Studio freezes.
cards.tryit: Make a platform that disappears for 3 seconds, then comes back, forever. Jump across it!

cards.title: React to a touch
cards.front: How does the door know you walked up?
cards.back: Every part has a Touched event. door.Touched:Connect(open) runs open whenever something bumps it. Open, wait 3 seconds, close. Note the colon before Connect!
cards.tryit: Make your door open when touched and close after 3 seconds. Test it with your avatar.

words.d: A text file of code that tells your game what to do.
A name you give to a value so you can reuse it.
A setting of a part, like its colour or see-through amount.
A named block of code you can run whenever you want.
Something that happens in the game, like a touch, that code can react to.

quiz.q: Your script is inside a Part. What does script.Parent point to?
opts: The Part the script is inside
quiz.hint: Think about a family tree in the Explorer. Who holds the script?
quiz.why: Parent is whatever the script sits inside, so here it's the Part.

quiz.q: Your vanishing platform loop makes Studio freeze. What's missing?
quiz.hint: A loop that never pauses never lets Studio do anything else.
quiz.why: Without task.wait(), the loop runs nonstop and the game never gets a turn.

quiz.q: Your door looks closed, but players walk right through it. Which property should be true?
quiz.hint: One property is about looks, one about falling, one about bumping into things.
quiz.why: CanCollide decides if players bump into a part or pass through it.

opts: Opens the door once, right now
Runs open whenever something touches the door
quiz.hint: Touched is an event. What do events wait for?
quiz.why: Connect links the event to your function, so it runs on every touch.
